bug_semantics: soup_message_headers_set_content_disposition() concatenates a caller-controlled disposition type and params (for example filename) in set_content_foo() and stores the result as Content-Disposition. After the soup3 common-header fast path, that store goes through soup_message_headers_replace_common() -> soup_message_headers_append_common(), which copies the value verbatim with no CR/LF rejection. soup_message_headers_append() / replace() still reject values containing \r or \n. The injected CRLF is later serialized as part of the HTTP request or response, enabling unauthenticated header injection / HTTP response splitting (CWE-93).
flaw_origin: The Content-Disposition setter originally stored via soup_message_headers_replace(), which since 996b1562e7ae05e22ed7207a87951b97647e24ae (2009-04-05, Dan Winship) rejects CR/LF in header values. On 2021-06-03 Carlos Garcia Campos switched set_content_foo() from that validating replace() to the new unvalidated replace_common() in 732fcd4bb6899f8585f13789fadfc1de56c4a879 ('Use header fast paths internally whenever possible'). The immediate parent 18ef5ed9166914334e0c107d251525a6d082722e still calls replace(); append_common() itself was added there without a value check, but Content-Disposition was not wired to that sink until 732fcd4. That first write of the bypass is the BIC: a single-parent non-squash commit, not a move of already-vulnerable lines.
